dataset.author: Alexander F. Wagner
dataset.title: Leverage Beyond Debt: Evidence from the AI Build-Out (data)

changes: Selected one contract and its instrument; original CSV string values retained as JSON, including blanks. Other arrangements omitted; attribution, hashes and evidence locators added. No endorsement implied. SEC company disclosures are not relicensed under the dataset license.

contracts.beneficiary: unnamed cloud service provider (= Nebius per NBIS 6-K $15bn unsold-capacity commitment)
contracts.instrument_type: contingent cloud-capacity purchase commitment - reduced "if the cloud service provider is able to sell such capacity to other customers"
contracts.notes: CROSS-FILING IDENTITY RESOLUTION: Meta's unnamed $14.72bn backstop = Nebius's disclosed $15bn Meta unsold-capacity commitment (HL-0034); non-cancelable commitments total $349.3bn (from $131bn) | [reduction mechanism (counterparty sales to others), not a termination right: 'shrinks as provider sells to others']

instruments.trigger_or_contingency: capacity NOT sold to third-party customers
instruments.notes: CROSS-FILING PAIR: Nebius discloses $15bn commitment; Meta discloses $14.72bn contingent obligation reduced as provider sells to others; demand insurance customer->supplier; binds when demand is weak; the edge carries Meta's 14.72, the writer's own filing (decision 3, CU-5); Nebius's 15 is the fact nbis_meta_unsold_capacity
instruments.ladder_component: Contingent cloud-capacity purchase obligation (backstop; = Nebius per HL-0047)
instruments.ladder_basis: in-force contingent obligation 'to purchase up to $14.72 billion of cloud capacity over a five-year period, which may be reduced if the cloud service provider is able to sell such capacity to other customers' - Meta cannot cancel; binds in full when third-party demand is absent (wrong-way)
instruments.coverage_note: pays when capacity is not sold to third parties
instruments.clause_instrument: contingent purchase of a cloud provider's unsold capacity (the Nebius backstop)
instruments.clause_trigger: the capacity is not sold to other customers
instruments.clause_note: the payment buys the unsold capacity at the contract price; no asset or lease changes hands; the cap is Meta's figure (Nebius states up to 15)
instruments.date_note: Firmed: first quantified in the 10-Q filed 2026-04-30 ('contingent obligations to purchase up to $14.72 billion of cloud capacity', meta-20260331.txt L475); absent from the 10-K filed 2026-01-29

evidence_locators.field: HL-0047 termination_right = `not disclosed` (Meta, contingent cloud-capacity purchase commitment ($14.72bn))
